messages.author: 72c025ccfc1fb009
messages.subject: NA/NaN warning
parts:
I have an assessment model that compiles fine and when I run it using nlminb() I get a warning in R (this is after it estimates through many parameters, I can tell by setting tracepar = TRUE).

Warning messages:
1: In nlminb(start = obj$par, objective = obj$fn, gradient = obj$gr,  :
  NA/NaN function evaluation

When I look at the nlminb object it says the optimisation converged and I also get a sensible hessian. So I am currently taking the approach of ignoring the warning. I have tried finding the parameters that
would cause the Na/NaN but no luck. I just wanted to ask the community if this was a common issue? whether I should be more concerned about it than I currently am?

Cheers.

messages.author: 395bdca538bcae5d
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] NA/NaN warning
parts: I've seen this with my models too, where there is no obvious 'bad' part of the likelihood surface that is undefined. I always assumed it was something like overflow on an exponentiated parameter on its path to convergence and thus ignored it. But I have nothing to back that up. Anyone else have deeper insights? -Cole

messages.author: 02e03030784aa6a7
messages.subject: Re: NA/NaN warning
parts:
I agree. On its way to the minimum, nlminb() visits some part of the parameter space where the objective
function is not well defined. This is not a problem if convergence in the end is OK. I guess
tracepar = TRUE can help you find out for which parameter value this happened, and hence
teach you something about the structure of your model.

messages.author: 72c025ccfc1fb009
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Re: NA/NaN warning
parts:
Thought I would comment on this for future users, if you want to find the combination of parameters that cause a NA/NaN during an optimization I have I used the following code.


options(warn = 2); # any warning gets upgraded to an error and so will kick out of optim() or nlminb() if encountered.
obj = MakeADFun(...)
opt = nlminb(obj$par, obj$fn, obj$gr)
# Error in nlminb(mod_2$par, mod_2$fn, mod_2$gr ...)
#(converted from warning) NA/NaN function evaluation
obj$env$last.par

messages.author: 395bdca538bcae5d
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Re: NA/NaN warning
parts:
Hi Craig, thanks for following up. That is indeed a good tip and I just used it today. However I had something strange happen. When the model crashes with NaN gradient

Error in nlminb(start = startpar, objective = fn, gradient = gr, control = control,  :
(converted from warning) NA/NaN function evaluation

I then pass that last.par through and as expected get NaN for both fn and gr

all <- Obj$env$last.par
fixed <- all[-Obj$env$random]
Obj$fn(fixed)
Obj$gr(fixed)

However, when I run the report and extract the objective function (jnll) it is not NaN!

> Obj$report(all)$jnll
[1] 70987.23

This NLL is about what the starting values are, i.e., not great but not outrageous. How is it possible that fn() returns NaN but report()$nll is valid? I assume there is something weird going on with the LA? When I take the trace output and put it back through the model to get a fn and max(abs(gr)) values the NLL decreases as expected but the gradients are not reliable. 

I'm experimenting with MCMC but thought I'd ask if anyone else has experienced such strange behavior.

messages.author: 90b303eef43fd993
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Re: NA/NaN warning
parts:
Cole, the reason is that 'Obj$fn(fixed)' is the marginal likelihood obtained using the LA. LA returns NaN because the inner hessian matrix is singular (determinant=0). That's why this really is a problem with the LA: The marginal likelihood, determined by LA, becomes infinite when the outer parameters are tuned in a way such that singularity occurs. nlminb always ends up with a crazy value because it gets attracted by the worst possible point(s) in the parameter space where LA is most inaccurate!
In contrast 'Obj$report(all)$jnll' returns the joint negative log likelihood which is finite. There is no contradiction.
